session.question: How do digital tools in environmental education foster sustainability awareness among learners?
session.answer:
Digital tools foster sustainability awareness by making environmental and sustainability concepts more interactive, experiential, and accessible. Across reviewed studies, tools such as virtual reality, augmented reality, digital games, and other digital learning resources improved environmental learning gains and increased students’ concern for planetary sustainability. These tools appear to strengthen awareness by helping learners engage directly with environmental issues, especially climate change and other sustainability challenges, rather than receiving information passively. (hajjhassan2024environmentaleducationa chunk 1)

A key mechanism is experiential learning. Digital simulations and game-based formats allow students to explore real-world policy, ecological, and management scenarios in a controlled setting, which deepens understanding of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and improves both knowledge and attitudes toward sustainable development. In the reviewed board-game study, the digital version was more effective than the non-digital version in improving sustainability-related outcomes. (ho2022applyinggamebasedexperiential chunk 1)

Digital tools also support sustainability awareness by reducing reliance on resource-intensive field activities and replacing them with low-impact immersive alternatives. In horticulture and landscape management education, AR/VR enabled hybrid and collaborative learning while linking environmental topics to practical decision-making, thereby promoting environmentally conscious learning. (kee2022digitalexperientiallearning chunk 1)

Finally, algorithmic tools such as knowledge graphs and recommendation systems can organize sustainability content, improve teaching effectiveness, and guide learners toward relevant environmental literacy resources, further reinforcing sustainability-oriented learning pathways. (hu2023environmentalliteracyeducation chunk 1)

session.context:
pqac-99c4844c: The review reports that evidence-based studies in environmental education suggest digital tools can improve environmental learning gains and strengthen sustainability awareness among students. In the 21 articles reviewed (2013–2023), virtual reality tools and climate change topics were especially common. Overall, the findings indicate that using digital tools has a positive impact on students’ concern for the sustainability of the planet, helping foster greater awareness of environmental issues and sustainability challenges among learners.
From Mira Hajj-Hassan, Rawad Chaker, and Anne‐Marie Cederqvist. Environmental education: a systematic review on the use of digital tools for fostering sustainability awareness. Sustainability, 2024. URL: https://doi.org/10.3390/su16093733, doi:10.3390/su16093733.

pqac-ae95332f: The paper explains that game-based experiential learning can deepen public understanding of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) by making learners understand their relevance through a board game that simulates real-world national and international policies. To adapt to COVID-era digital instruction, the authors created a digital version of the board game and compared it with a non-digital version. Using a comprehensive sustainability questionnaire, they found both versions improved students’ knowledge and attitudes toward sustainable development, with the digital game being more effective. This suggests digital tools in environmental education foster sustainability awareness by engaging learners interactively and improving both understanding and attitudes.
From Shin-Jia Ho, Yu-Shan Hsu, Chien-Hung Lai, Fong-Han Chen, and Ming‐Hour Yang. Applying game-based experiential learning to comprehensive sustainable development-based education. Sustainability, 2022. URL: https://doi.org/10.3390/su14031172, doi:10.3390/su14031172.

pqac-00b4833b: The paper explains that immersive digital tools such as augmented reality (AR) and virtual reality (VR) were used in higher education horticulture and landscape management to replace or supplement field studies during COVID-19. Based on student survey results, these tools supported team-based hybrid learning and experiential learning aligned with Kolb’s cycle. The authors argue that AR/VR simulation can make tree management instruction more environmentally sustainable by reducing the need for physical site visits while also promoting a more environmentally conscious, collaborative, and innovative learning experience. This suggests digital tools foster sustainability awareness by linking environmental topics with interactive, practical, and low-impact learning methods.
From Tris Kee and Hao Zhang. Digital experiential learning for sustainable horticulture and landscape management education. Sustainability, 2022. URL: https://doi.org/10.3390/su14159116, doi:10.3390/su14159116.

pqac-da0767e9: The excerpt describes a game-based experiential learning approach for sustainability education. It says a board game was designed to simulate the real world, including national and international policies, so students could understand the relevance of the SDGs through experiential learning (Kolb’s theory). A digital version was created during COVID-19, and both digital and non-digital versions improved students’ knowledge and attitudes toward sustainable development, with the digital version being more effective. The study used a comprehensive evaluation questionnaire to measure knowledge and attitudes. This suggests mechanisms such as interactive simulation, experiential engagement, and digital delivery can increase sustainability awareness and attitude change.
From Shin-Jia Ho, Yu-Shan Hsu, Chien-Hung Lai, Fong-Han Chen, and Ming‐Hour Yang. Applying game-based experiential learning to comprehensive sustainable development-based education. Sustainability, 2022. URL: https://doi.org/10.3390/su14031172, doi:10.3390/su14031172.

pqac-71315ccd: The excerpt describes a study on environmental literacy education and sustainable development in schools. It proposes an evaluation index system for teaching effectiveness, uses fuzzy comprehensive evaluation, and builds a curriculum knowledge model from a knowledge graph of environmental literacy education. It also applies a recommendation method based on user knowledge transfer to recommend educational resources. The abstract says experimental results verify these methods are effective. Overall, the paper suggests digital/algorithmic tools like knowledge graphs and resource recommendation systems can support environmental education by organizing knowledge, improving teaching effectiveness, and guiding learners toward sustainability-related content.
From Huang Hu and Chun Te Hsin. Environmental literacy education and sustainable development in schools based on teaching effectiveness. International Journal of Sustainable Development and Planning, 2023. URL: https://doi.org/10.18280/ijsdp.180535, doi:10.18280/ijsdp.180535.

session.formatted_answer:
Question: How do digital tools in environmental education foster sustainability awareness among learners?

Digital tools foster sustainability awareness by making environmental and sustainability concepts more interactive, experiential, and accessible. Across reviewed studies, tools such as virtual reality, augmented reality, digital games, and other digital learning resources improved environmental learning gains and increased students’ concern for planetary sustainability. These tools appear to strengthen awareness by helping learners engage directly with environmental issues, especially climate change and other sustainability challenges, rather than receiving information passively. (hajjhassan2024environmentaleducationa chunk 1)

A key mechanism is experiential learning. Digital simulations and game-based formats allow students to explore real-world policy, ecological, and management scenarios in a controlled setting, which deepens understanding of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and improves both knowledge and attitudes toward sustainable development. In the reviewed board-game study, the digital version was more effective than the non-digital version in improving sustainability-related outcomes. (ho2022applyinggamebasedexperiential chunk 1)

Digital tools also support sustainability awareness by reducing reliance on resource-intensive field activities and replacing them with low-impact immersive alternatives. In horticulture and landscape management education, AR/VR enabled hybrid and collaborative learning while linking environmental topics to practical decision-making, thereby promoting environmentally conscious learning. (kee2022digitalexperientiallearning chunk 1)

Finally, algorithmic tools such as knowledge graphs and recommendation systems can organize sustainability content, improve teaching effectiveness, and guide learners toward relevant environmental literacy resources, further reinforcing sustainability-oriented learning pathways. (hu2023environmentalliteracyeducation chunk 1)
